blocks.text: Network security protects computer networks and keeps data safe from unauthorised access. It helps prevent data loss and damage, protects personal and important information, stops hackers from entering, and protects devices from malware. Many users connect to networks every day, so every network, at home or in an organisation, needs basic security measures.

blocks.title: Class activity
blocks.text: Discuss how security protects sensitive data, such as patients' CT scans in a hospital.

blocks.caption: Network security tools
rows: A security device or program that controls incoming and outgoing traffic. It blocks harmful or unwanted data and acts as a barrier between safe and unsafe networks; used in homes and offices.
Changes data into a secret form that only authorised users can read. It protects data during transfer, for example in email and online banking, and prevents data theft.
Decides who can use the network: only authorised users may enter. Usernames and passwords are common access controls, and permissions limit what each user can do.

blocks.alt: On the left a cloud labelled Internet. In the middle a red brick wall labelled firewall: rules for traffic in and out. A green arrow labelled allowed traffic passes through the wall into a green box labelled private network containing a computer, a laptop and a server. A red arrow labelled harmful traffic hits the wall and is turned back, labelled blocked.
blocks.caption: A firewall between the Internet and a private network (original diagram after Fig 1.17).
blocks.long_description: The firewall checks each piece of traffic against its rules: what is allowed passes, and what matches a harmful pattern is stopped before it reaches the private network.

items: Phishing tricks users into sharing information.
Denial of Service (DoS) attacks stop network services.

blocks.text: Security tools such as firewalls, encryption and access control reduce these threats.
